key_insight: The paper benchmarks four operator-learning surrogates for aerodynamics and finds that Bi-Stride Multi-Scale Graph Neural Network and Transolver(++) are the most promising for predicting pressure fields on airfoils and aircraft.
engineering_relevance: These models could reduce CFD cost for design optimization and load analysis by approximating pressure distributions across many geometries and flow conditions.
method: Tested 2D airfoils of varying complexity and a 3D industrial aircraft configuration
Assessed shock capture, scalability to large meshes, and performance under data scarcity
evidence_signal: The evaluation spans two experiments on aerodynamic pressure prediction, focusing on surface pressure distributions and comparing model behavior across discontinuities, mesh size, and limited training data.
watch_item: Performance depends on architecture and problem setting, so these surrogates still need careful validation before deployment on new geometries or flow regimes.
paper_title: Evaluation of State-of-the-Art Deep Learning Architectures for Aerodynamical Predictions
